summary: The v1 record is right about the conclusion and wrong about how it was reached. Star Fleet's extremalSize does denote the same quantity as Formal Conjectures' Erdos321.R at the pinned commit. It is not established by four pairwise-identical definitions: one of the four pairs is a one-way implication, and the file the v1 record read contains two fixed statements it said were not there.
why_corrected: v1 recorded `Admissible A` and `A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N` as the same predicate. `Admissible N A := A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ Valid A` is a conjunction, so `Admissible N A → A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N` holds and the converse does not. The bridge v1 gave — 'both range over subsets of Finset.Icc 1 N' — does not mention the second conjunct, and that conjunct is already pair 1.

v1 said, unqualified, that there is no fixed formal statement here to be faithful to. FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/321.lean at 59f30aa3 carries `erdos_321.variants.lower` and `erdos_321.variants.upper`, both `@[category research solved]`, both complete statements about `R N` with no `answer(sorry)`. The unqualified sentence is false; the statement it should have made is that no fixed formal statement of the *open* question exists.

formal_statement.definition: R (N : ℕ) : ℕ := sSup { #A | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ : Set.InjOn (fun (S : Finset ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℚ) / n) A.powerset) }
formal_statement.open_placeholder: The open declarations state `answer(sorry)` on the right: `erdos_321` itself and the `isTheta`, `isBigO` and `isLittleO` variants. No fixed formal statement of the open question exists at this commit.

solved_variants_present.content: The Bleicher–Erdős two-sided bound on R N, stated in full with no placeholder.
solved_variants_present.not_compared: This record does not compare the Star Fleet terminal theorem against either. Both are two-sided bounds on the same quantity, so the comparison is worth making and has not been made.

denotational_correspondence.conclusion: extremalSize N = R N at these commits.

established_by.formal_conjectures: fun S => ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℚ) / n
established_by.bridge: (n : ℚ)⁻¹ and (1 : ℚ) / n are the same rational for every n.

established_by.starfleet: Valid A := ∀ S ∈ A.powerset, ∀ T ∈ A.powerset, reciprocalSubsetSum S = reciprocalSubsetSum T → S = T
established_by.formal_conjectures: Set.InjOn (fun S => ∑ n ∈ S, (1 : ℚ) / n) A.powerset
established_by.bridge: Injectivity on the powerset written as a double quantifier is the definition of Set.InjOn on that set, and the summands agree by the pair above.

established_by.starfleet: Admissible N A := A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ Valid A
established_by.formal_conjectures: the two side conditions of the set-builder: A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, and Set.InjOn … A.powerset
established_by.bridge: Admissible is the conjunction of both side conditions, not either one alone. v1 paired it against the subset condition only, which is a one-way implication.
established_by.note: This pair is not independent of the one above it: its second conjunct is that pair.

established_by.formal_conjectures: R N := sSup of the same cardinalities
established_by.bridge: The family is finite and contains ∅, so a Finset.sup and the supremum of the same set of cardinalities agree — including at N where the family is a singleton {∅}, where both are 0.

denotational_correspondence.count_correction: Three distinct correspondences plus the conjunction that combines two of them. v1 reported four independent pairs.

three_gates.machine_proof_gate: The project builds under its pinned toolchain and the kernel accepts the terminal theorem. Unchanged from v1.
three_gates.definition_gate: extremalSize and R denote the same quantity, by the correspondences above. The conclusion is unchanged from v1; the derivation is corrected.
three_gates.statement_gate: Inconclusive against the open question, whose declarations all carry `answer(sorry)`. Not assessed against the two solved variants, which are fixed statements of the same shape and were not compared.

does_not_establish: That Erdos problem 321 is resolved. It is open, and this repository takes no position on it.
That the bound is optimal, or that it is the answer the `answer(sorry)` placeholders are waiting for.
That the terminal theorem does or does not match `erdos_321.variants.lower` or `erdos_321.variants.upper`. That comparison was not performed by this record or by v1.
That the Lean development contains an error. Nothing here questions its soundness.
That the pinned Mathlib and toolchain are free of admitted declarations outside the audited dependency cone.
That any Formal Conjectures file other than 321.lean was read.
